_comment: R227 identity pairs (R75 format), 2026-10-16, Claude Opus 5.5, written from the NTSB corpus text only; no build output opened.

evidence.quote: # Beech A36 accidents investigated by the NTSB
A National Transportation Safety Board Pilot/Operator Aircraft Accident/Incident Report was not received from the right seat pilot.

identity_pairs.note: One organisation: the abbreviation in the Beech heading and the full name in the Piper report CEN22LA249. Trap: abbreviation vs full name across documents.

names: National Transportation Safety Board Pilot/Operator Aircraft Accident/Incident Report Form 6120.1

evidence.quote: In the recommendation section of the NTSB Accident/Incident Reporting Form 6120.1, the pilot stated
The pilot did not submit the National Transportation Safety Board Pilot/Operator Aircraft Accident/Incident Report Form 6120.1.

identity_pairs.note: One document type, the NTSB pilot report form 6120.1, written two ways (Beech ANC21LA027, Robinson CEN21LA339). Same form number decides it; the wording differs.

evidence.quote: The student pilot reported that he was 0n a solo cross-country flight
The student pilot’s loss of directional control during landing which resulted in an impact with a snowbank.

identity_pairs.note: One person: the solo student pilot of Cessna CEN21LA126 in the narrative and in that accident's probable cause (the snowbank ties the two).

names: The pilot in the right seat

evidence.quote: The pilot in the right seat was flying and rotated 1,000 ft down the runway
A National Transportation Safety Board Pilot/Operator Aircraft Accident/Incident Report was not received from the right seat pilot.

identity_pairs.note: One person in Piper CEN22LA249: the right-seat pilot, who was flying, written two ways.

names: The pilot in the airplane’s left seat

evidence.quote: The pilot in the airplane’s left seat reported that they were taking off from a turf runway
The left seat pilot reported that there were no preaccident mechanical malfunctions

identity_pairs.note: One person in Piper CEN22LA249: the left-seat pilot (the one who reported), written two ways.

evidence.quote: Examination revealed that all compressor turbine (CT) rotor blades were fractured at varying spanwise locations.
Metallurgical analysis of the CT blades revealed micro-voids
Fracture of the compressor turbine (CT) blades due to creep.

identity_pairs.note: One part set in Air Tractor CEN22LA312: the compressor turbine blades, written in full, with 'rotor', and as the abbreviation CT.

evidence.quote: he elected to activate the Cirrus airframe parachute system.
which led to the pilot’s decision to activate the airframe parachute system.

identity_pairs.note: One system on the Cirrus of CEN21LA232, with and without the maker's name (narrative vs probable cause).

evidence.quote: the pilot switched back to the left fuel tank and then focused his attention on maintaining airplane control
the fuel venting system on the left-wing fuel tank was obstructed by what appeared to be insect debris.
The blockage of the left fuel tank vent

identity_pairs.note: One tank of the Beech A36 in CEN23LA344, written 'left fuel tank' and 'left-wing fuel tank'.

evidence.quote: The pilot realized he had struck a wire as the helicopter pitched up and started to slow.
the pilot observed the wire wrapped around the helicopter.

identity_pairs.note: One wire in Robinson CEN21LA339: first introduced as 'a wire', then 'the wire' wrapped round the helicopter.

evidence.quote: The commercial pilot reported that before the aerial application flight, he added Jet A fuel to both wing tanks
The pilot performed a forced landing to a bean field.

identity_pairs.note: One person in Air Tractor CEN21LA362: introduced with his certificate ('commercial pilot'), then 'the pilot'. Trap: a qualifier added to a generic word.

evidence.quote: The pilot performed a forced landing to a bean field.
The property owner of the bean field reported that he helped the pilot add about 9 gallons

identity_pairs.note: One field in Air Tractor CEN21LA362: the forced-landing site and the field whose owner helped refuel.

evidence.quote: The engine had recently been installed by maintenance personnel
The failure of maintenance personnel to properly torque a fuel line “B” nut

identity_pairs.note: The same maintenance personnel of Cessna CEN22LA194 (engine installation; probable cause). Not the maintenance personnel of CEN22LA244, who examined a different airplane.

evidence.quote: he began receiving conflicting information from the flight instruments and digital flight information display.
After determining that he could not rely on the information from the flight instruments

identity_pairs.note: The same instruments of the Cirrus in CEN21LA232, twice in one paragraph.

evidence.quote: The flight instructor told the student pilot to break off the maneuver and apply engine power
The flight instructor declared an emergency and executed a forced landing to a park area

identity_pairs.note: Two people: the instructor of CEN21LA414 (LaSalle, CO) and the instructor of CEN22LA194 (Traverse City, MI). Trap: identical generic role in one document.

evidence.quote: A flight instructor, who flew the airplane earlier in the day, reported that he heard a noise
Except for the noise the pilot heard, he reported no other mechanical malfunctions

identity_pairs.note: Two people in one accident, Cessna CEN22LA244: the instructor flew the airplane earlier that day; the pilot flew the accident flight.

evidence.quote: The pilot receiving instruction was on a visual approach to the runway during an instructional flight
The flight instructor took control of the airplane and made multiple attempts to restart the engine

identity_pairs.note: Two people in Cessna CEN22LA194: the trainee and the instructor who took control. Trap: both are 'pilots' of one flight.

evidence.quote: The student pilot reported that he was 0n a solo cross-country flight
The student pilot reported that he was performing a touch and go landing during a solo traffic pattern flight

identity_pairs.note: Two people: the Cessna student of CEN21LA126 (Urbana, OH) and the Piper student of CEN23LA026 (Mesquite, TX). Trap: identical name and sentence frame across documents.

evidence.quote: On short final a pilot-rated passenger seated in the right front seat recommended adding power.
The pilot assumed this was to “cushion” the landing

identity_pairs.note: Two people in Beech ANC21LA027: the passenger who holds a pilot rating and the pilot flying. Trap: 'pilot' inside the passenger's name.

evidence.quote: The left seat pilot reported that there were no preaccident mechanical malfunctions
The pilot in the right seat was flying and rotated 1,000 ft down the runway

identity_pairs.note: Two people in one airplane, Piper CEN22LA249: the left-seat pilot reported, the right-seat pilot flew. Trap: same role word, one seat apart.

evidence.quote: The airplane banked left, with the left-wing tip striking the ground.
The airplane subsequently impacted a fence off the end of the runway

identity_pairs.note: Two aircraft: the Cirrus of CEN21FA299 (Lamoni, IA) and the Cirrus of CEN22LA235 (Nashville, AR). Trap: same model, same word, different accidents.

evidence.quote: It is likely the pilot failed to identify the rising terrain in time to clear the trees.
the pilot felt the right wing rapidly dip and he applied left aileron to correct it.

identity_pairs.note: Two people: the pilot of Air Tractor CEN21LA283 (Edwardsburg, MI) and the pilot of CEN22LA310 (Wyoming, IL).

evidence.quote: The airplane’s right wing was bent up at the tip resulting in substantial damage.
Postaccident examination of the airplane revealed substantial damage to the right wing and engine mount.

identity_pairs.note: Two wings of two Cessnas: CEN21LA126 (snowbank) and CEN22LA194 (forced landing in a park).

evidence.quote: the engine began to shake and lost total power.
A test run of the engine was subsequently conducted and the engine ran at various power settings

identity_pairs.note: Two engines: the failed engine of Beech CEN21LA221 (fractured connecting rods) and the engine of CEN21LA382 that test-ran normally.

evidence.quote: he felt the helicopter begin to settle.
The helicopter touched down hard onto the runway surface.

identity_pairs.note: Two helicopters: the Robinson of ANC21LA079 (Pelican, AK) and the one of CEN21LA284 (Reserve, LA).

evidence.quote: Postaccident examination of the engine revealed that connecting rods 2 through 5 were fractured and separated from the crankshaft
The connecting rod bearings number 1 and 6 displayed significant scoring consistent with a lack of oil lubrication.

identity_pairs.note: Two different part groups in one engine (Beech CEN21LA221): rods 2-5 vs bearings 1 and 6. Trap: shared head word 'connecting rod'.

evidence.quote: Examination revealed that all compressor turbine (CT) rotor blades were fractured at varying spanwise locations.
The power turbine (PT) rotor blades downstream of the CT blades exhibited impact damage

identity_pairs.note: Two blade sets of one engine in Air Tractor CEN22LA312: CT blades failed by creep, PT blades downstream were damaged by them.

evidence.quote: the airplane struck an airport perimeter fence that resulted in substantial damaged to both wings.
During the forced landing, the airplane impacted terrain and a perimeter fence.

identity_pairs.note: Two fences: at the airport of Air Tractor CEN22LA312 (Decatur, IL) and at the park of Cessna CEN22LA194 (Traverse City, MI).
